title: Resolve target names through a SOCKS proxy
goal: Send a target hostname to a SOCKS5 proxy for resolution and connection; use when the proxy knows the target, preserving the working .NET 10 socks5 spelling and checking failures.

sdk.reason: Build net11.0 against .NET 11 references; exact SDK11 RC2 is a separate tested baseline.
sdk.name: .NET SDK

runtime.reason: The newer proxy spelling/automatic decoder requires the .NET 11 SocketsHttpHandler implementation.
runtime.name: .NET

language.name: C#
language.reason: Canonical net11.0 project explicitly selects C#15.0; the proxy API does not itself require new language syntax. This is the configured example route, not a minimum-language claim.

packageAssets: Framework System.Net.Http/System.Net.Primitives; no NuGet backport route.
prerequisites: Nullable/implicit-usings net11.0 application; copy canonical types into the same assembly.
Reachable trusted SOCKS5 proxy and target hostname retained in request URI; loopback controlled mapping used for proof.
platforms: SocketsHttpHandler on CoreCLR; Windows x64 executed, browser/mobile native handlers and other operating systems unverified.
providers: Controlled SOCKS5 server; no cloud/account/service SDK.
stabilityLimitations: Actual RC2 verification, not final-GA proof; PIN-962 and PIN-959 remain open.
constraints: Keep socks5 on .NET 10: its hostname forwarding already works; socks5h is a newer alias.
Hostname forwarding is not global DNS-leak prevention; proxy credentials/transport, origin TLS and bypass/redirect policy remain separate.

selectionNotes: Keep socks5 on .NET 10: its hostname forwarding already works; socks5h is a newer alias.

evidence.scope: Real Windows x64 SOCKS5 hostname CONNECT, actual loopback target response, authentication success/failure, no acceptable method, refused CONNECT and cancelled negotiation; local negative DNS and old alias rejection. No global DNS privacy, production proxy, other-platform or GA proof.
